title: Second Largest Distinct
statement: Given a list of integers, return the second largest DISTINCT value. If there are fewer than two distinct values, return None.

title: Run-Length Encode
statement: Compress a string by replacing each maximal run of the same character with the character followed by the run length, e.g. 'aaab' -> 'a3b1'. The empty string maps to the empty string.

title: Balanced Brackets
statement: Return True if every bracket in s is properly matched and nested. Brackets are (), [] and {}. All other characters are ignored.

title: Longest Unique Substring
statement: Return the length of the longest contiguous substring of s that contains no repeated characters.

title: Merge Intervals
statement: Given a list of closed intervals [start, end] with start <= end, merge all overlapping or touching intervals (e.g. [1,3] and [3,5] merge) and return the result sorted by start.

title: Coin Change Ways
signature: def coin_ways(coins: list[int], amount: int) -> int:
statement: Count the number of different multisets of coins (order does not matter) that sum to amount. Each coin value may be used any number of times. coins contains distinct positive integers. coin_ways(coins, 0) is 1.

title: Grid Islands
statement: grid is a list of equal-length strings made of '#' (land) and '.' (water). Count the islands: maximal groups of land cells connected horizontally or vertically (not diagonally).

title: Digit Root Steps
statement: Multiplicative persistence: count how many times you must replace a non-negative integer n by the product of its decimal digits until it becomes a single digit. A single-digit n needs 0 steps.

title: Kth Smallest Pair Sum
signature: def kth_pair_sum(a: list[int], b: list[int], k: int) -> int:
statement: Given two non-empty lists a and b of integers, consider all len(a)*len(b) sums a[i] + b[j]. Return the k-th smallest of these sums (1-indexed, counting duplicates). 1 <= k <= len(a)*len(b).

title: Word Frequency Top K
signature: def top_k_words(text: str, k: int) -> list[str]:
statement: Split text into words (maximal runs of letters a-z, case-insensitive, converted to lowercase). Return the k most frequent words, ordered by descending count, ties broken alphabetically. If there are fewer than k distinct words, return all of them.
reference_solution:
import re
from collections import Counter

def top_k_words(text, k):
    c = Counter(re.findall(r'[a-z]+', text.lower()))
    return [w for w, _ in sorted(c.items(), key=lambda t: (-t[1], t[0]))[:k]]
test_inputs: A a a b B c

title: Spiral Order
statement: Return the elements of a rectangular matrix in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left corner and moving right first. An empty matrix (or one with empty rows) gives an empty list.
reference_solution:
def spiral(matrix):
    out = []
    m = [row[:] for row in matrix]
    while m and m[0]:
        out += m.pop(0)
        m = [list(r) for r in zip(*m)][::-1]
    return out

title: Edit Distance
signature: def edit_distance(a: str, b: str) -> int:
statement: Return the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions or substitutions needed to turn string a into string b (Levenshtein distance).

title: Bit Count Range
statement: For every integer i from 0 to n inclusive, compute the number of 1 bits in the binary representation of i. Return the list of these counts. n >= 0.
reference_solution:
def bits_upto(n):
    return [bin(i).count('1') for i in range(n + 1)]

title: Minimum Platforms
statement: Each meeting is [start, end) with start < end (end is exclusive, so a meeting ending at 5 frees its room for one starting at 5). Return the minimum number of rooms needed so that no two meetings in the same room overlap.

title: Roman to Integer
statement: Convert a valid Roman numeral (characters I, V, X, L, C, D, M, using standard subtractive notation like IV and CM) to its integer value.

title: Shortest Path in Maze
statement: maze is a list of equal-length strings with '.' open, '#' wall, exactly one 'S' start and one 'E' end. Moving one cell up/down/left/right costs 1 step. Return the minimum number of steps from S to E, or -1 if E is unreachable.

title: Parse Arithmetic
statement: Evaluate an integer expression with non-negative integer literals, +, -, *, parentheses and spaces. * binds tighter than + and -, which are left-associative. There is no unary minus. The input is always well-formed.

title: Rotate String Check
signature: def is_rotation(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
statement: Return True if string b can be obtained by moving some prefix of string a to its end (a rotation, including rotating by 0). Two empty strings are rotations of each other.
reference_solution:
def is_rotation(a, b):
    return len(a) == len(b) and b in a + a

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
statement: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of nums (elements need not be contiguous).

title: Group Anagrams Count
statement: Two words are in the same group if one is a rearrangement of the other's letters (same multiset of characters, case-sensitive). Return the number of distinct groups among the given words.
reference_solution:
def anagram_groups(words):
    return len({''.join(sorted(w)) for w in words})

title: Josephus Survivor
signature: def survivor(n: int, k: int) -> int:
statement: n people stand in a circle numbered 1..n. Starting from person 1, count k people around the circle (person 1 counts as 1); the k-th person is removed, and counting restarts from the next person. Return the number of the last person remaining. n >= 1, k >= 1.

title: Valid Sudoku Row Col Box
statement: board is 9 strings of 9 characters, digits '1'-'9' or '.' for empty. Return True if no digit repeats within any row, any column, or any of the nine 3x3 boxes. Empty cells are ignored; the board need not be solvable.

title: Stock Profit With Cooldown
statement: prices[i] is a stock price on day i. You may complete as many buy-then-sell transactions as you like, holding at most one share at a time, but after selling you must wait one full day before buying again (cooldown). Return the maximum total profit.

title: Compress Ranges
statement: nums is sorted ascending with no duplicates. Summarise it as ranges of consecutive integers: a run a..b with a < b becomes 'a->b' and a single number becomes 'a'. Return the list of range strings in order.

title: Topological Order Exists
signature: def can_finish(n: int, prereqs: list[list[int]]) -> bool:
statement: There are n tasks labelled 0..n-1. Each pair [a, b] in prereqs means task b must be done before task a. Return True if all tasks can be completed (the dependency graph has no cycle).
reference_solution:
from collections import deque

def can_finish(n, prereqs):
    indeg = [0] * n
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for a, b in prereqs:
        adj[b].append(a)
        indeg[a] += 1
    q = deque(i for i in range(n) if indeg[i] == 0)
    done = 0
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        done += 1
        for v in adj[u]:
            indeg[v] -= 1
            if indeg[v] == 0:
                q.append(v)
    return done == n

title: Matrix Diagonal Sums
statement: Given a square matrix, return the sum of its main diagonal plus its anti-diagonal. When the size is odd, the centre element belongs to both diagonals but is counted only once.

title: Next Greater Element
statement: For each position i, find the first element to the right of i that is strictly greater than nums[i]; output that value, or -1 if none exists. Return the list of answers.

title: Unique Paths With Obstacles
statement: grid is a list of equal-length strings of '.' (free) and '#' (blocked). Count the paths from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell that move only right or down through free cells. If either corner is blocked the answer is 0.

title: Caesar Shift Words
signature: def shift_text(s: str, k: int) -> str:
statement: Shift every letter in s forward by k positions in the alphabet, wrapping around (z -> a), preserving case. Non-letters are unchanged. k can be negative or larger than 26.

title: Prime Factor Exponents
statement: Return the prime factorisation of an integer n >= 2 as a dict mapping each prime (written as a decimal string) to its exponent.
